public_sources.title: Larsson, Ramdas & Ruf, The numeraire e-variable and reverse information projection
public_sources.use: For every point alternative versus composite null a numeraire e-variable exists and is log-optimal. Section 7 proves universal inference q/p_max is inadmissible and the numeraire q/p* is pointwise at least as large because p*<=p_max.

public_sources.title: Wasserman, Ramdas & Balakrishnan, Universal Inference
public_sources.use: Finite-sample composite-null likelihood envelope underlying the retained r85 q_R/sup_C p factor.

results.claim: The r85 NIG universal factor has an exact reference-free standardized form. With n_ref=684, df=683, z=z_0.995, qlo=chi2_683(0.005), qhi=chi2_683(0.995), define h0=z*sqrt(df/qlo)/sqrt(n_ref)=0.10582811900240735, ell0=sqrt(df/qhi)=0.9345871297300398 and u0=sqrt(df/qlo)=1.074513925626049. For reference mean xbar_R and sample sd s_R, C_R=[xbar_R-h0*s_R,xbar_R+h0*s_R] x [ell0*s_R,u0*s_R], while the frozen NIG numerator has m0=xbar_R,kappa0=3,alpha0=3,beta0=2*s_R^2. Under z_i=(y_i-xbar_R)/s_R both numerator and every null block density contribute exactly s_R^{-m}, so E_UI is the same fixed function of standardized block sufficient statistics for every reference. The reference-good power envelope therefore reduces to transformed Gaussian alternatives d=(mu_Q-xbar_R)/s_R, v=sigma_Q^2/s_R^2 with xbar_R/s_R in [-h0,h0] and s_R in [sqrt(qlo/df),sqrt(qhi/df)].
results.impact: Continuum certification need not re-optimize the predictive/null envelope for every reference state; it can work on one fixed standardized block problem and a compact transformed-alternative domain.

results.claim: A new common-random engineering comparison used the same exact-KL=1 Gaussian post-change paths for r82, r84 and r85, two extremal reference-variance states s_R in {sqrt(qlo/df),sqrt(qhi/df)}, mean reference shifted toward the alternative until the true null mean is at the confidence-interval boundary, 11 variance-ratio directions spanning the full exact KL=1 shell, 250 paths per direction/reference endpoint, and post horizon 2048. To isolate late-start behavior without simulating a million null samples, every delayed-start recursion was conservatively initialized at the changepoint with A=0 and only its exact unstarted tail mass T_k; since live A is nonnegative this is a lower-state post-change stress, not a simulation of the full prechange process and not a false-alarm experiment.
results.paired_stress: A separate 150-path/scenario stream over all 11 directions, both reference endpoints and the five changepoint ages produced 16,500 paired path-scenarios. r85 was earlier/equal/later than r84 in 4268/12199/33 cases and earlier/equal/later than r82 in 10395/6105/0 cases. These are engineering comparisons only; continuum power and PFA still come from analytic/certification work.

results.claim: Conditional on any frozen reference R, the r85 block predictive q_R is a point alternative and P_R={N(mu,sigma^2)^m:(mu,sigma) in C_R} is a composite null. Larsson-Ramdas-Ruf therefore imply a numeraire X*_R=q_R/p*_R exists. Their Section 7 gives X*_R>=X_UI=q_R/p_max pointwise (strict on positive-measure sets in nondegenerate cases). If X*_R is evaluated as the same R-and-current-block function on deterministic nonoverlapping blocks, it is still a conditional e-factor, and all delayed starts share the same multiplier; the O(1) telescoping start-mixture compression is preserved. Thus r85's universal factor is a safe but provably non-optimal endpoint: an exact numeraire implementation could improve evidence without any pathwise power loss relative to r85.

Because r86a standardizes the problem once, a fixed candidate RIPr can be precomputed. Let p_Lbar be the equal mixture of the two Gaussian block laws at (mu,sigma)=(-h0,ell0),(+h0,ell0) and p_Ubar the equal mixture at (-h0,u0),(+h0,u0). A symmetric four-corner candidate p_rho=rho*p_Lbar+(1-rho)*p_Ubar was optimized on an independent NIG-predictive discovery stream. Deterministic hierarchical NIG quadrature (Gamma inverse-scale x Normal mean x chi-square residual) at orders 50x60x50 gave rho=0.5544174414300036 by solving E_q[p_Lbar/p_rho]=E_q[p_Ubar/p_rho]=1. The same quadrature gave E_q log(q/p_max) about 4.00667 nat/block and E_q log(q/p_rho) about 5.04957, a gain of about 1.04289 nat/block under q. Lower-order dense grids plus differential evolution put max_{(mu,sigma) in C0} E_q[p_{mu,sigma}/p_rho] at the four corners, numerically 1, with adjacent interior points materially below 1. An independent 500,000-sample validation gave active-corner expectations within about 0.002 of one and interior examples far below one.
results.status: Strong RIPr/numeraire candidate, not yet a continuum theorem. The quadrature/root/global-search layer is not interval-certified, so q/p_rho is not yet promoted as an e-factor. If a verified bound sup_C E_q[p_theta/p_rho]<=1+epsilon is obtained, q/((1+epsilon)p_rho) is immediately e-valid; if epsilon=0 is certified, Theorem 4.7 identifies the exact RIPr/numeraire candidate. Since p_rho is a convex mixture of null densities, p_rho<=p_max pointwise; without the continuum e-validity proof this gives only pointwise evidence dominance, not a valid replacement.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The matched validation initializes delayed-start accumulated wealth A=0 at the changepoint. It is deliberately a conservative tail-state post-change comparison and is not the distribution of a full detector conditioned on surviving a long null prefix.

The r85 factor still lacks a machine/continuum proof that its stated Chernoff miss bound covers every Gaussian KL>=1 direction and every reference-good state, although the new matched validation is strongly favorable.

The four-corner p_rho continuum constraint is supported by deterministic quadrature, dense search and independent Monte Carlo but is not analytically or interval certified. Do not call it an e-value, RIPr or numeraire yet.
Quadrature values are stable deterministic numerics, not directed-rounding enclosures.

All detector and RIPr claims remain restricted to clean iid Gaussian reference plus one fixed iid Gaussian step alternative and the frozen NIG block predictor. No heavy-tail, serial-dependence, gradual-drift or repeated-change guarantee follows.
frontier: Use Larsson-Ramdas-Ruf Theorem 4.7/Section 7 to certify or refute the four-corner candidate: prove C(mu,sigma)=E_q[p_{mu,sigma}/p_rho]<=1 over the entire standardized rectangle, or build an interval/transport certificate for a verified epsilon and scale the factor by 1+epsilon. Exploit the large numerical interior margin and exact symmetry before adding more mixture support.

Finish the r85 continuum power certificate using r86a's fixed standardized representation. Reduce the reference nuisance to the compact transformed Gaussian alternative domain instead of repeatedly optimizing raw reference mean/variance states.

If the four-corner candidate becomes e-valid, replace only the universal block factor first. Pointwise q/p_rho>=q/p_max means the resulting detector cannot be slower pathwise than r85 under identical weights/start recursion; then rerun common-random validation only to quantify the gain, not to establish safety.
Replace the chi-square/normal/quadrature numerical constants used in certification with directed-rounding interval enclosures if available; otherwise keep symbolic definitions authoritative.
exact_next_action: Prioritize a continuum validity proof for the standardized four-corner p_rho because it can strictly dominate the already favorable r85 UI factor without changing the delayed-start architecture. Write C(mu,sigma)=E_q[p_{mu,sigma}/p_rho] in the two sufficient statistics (block mean, centered SSE), exploit symmetry to restrict mu>=0, and prove boundary/corner maximality or interval-cover the compact rectangle. In parallel use the exact r86a location-scale reduction to close r85's KL>=1 Chernoff power surface. Promote p_rho only after a verified <=1 (or explicitly epsilon-scaled) continuum constraint; otherwise keep r85 and the r84 fallback unchanged.
